headline: Wyndham's profit rises despite a revenue pullback
summary_short: Wyndham's Q2 2026 net revenue fell 5.5% y/y to $375M as one-time conference pass-through revenue from a year ago rolled off and Revo-related fees were deferred, but operating income rose 16% to $174M and net income grew 17.2% to $102M ($1.36 diluted EPS) as expenses fell even faster than revenue.
summary_long: Net revenue fell 6% y/y on $20M lower conference-related pass-through revenue and $8M lower fees from Revo deferrals, partly offset by credit-card ancillary revenue and Revo-hotel management fees. Expenses fell 19% on the same comp and lower restructuring costs, lifting operating income 16% and net income 17% to $102M. Global RevPAR was roughly flat (-1% constant-currency): US +2% (Midwest, Texas, Florida, California strength) offset EMEA -6% (Mideast conflict, Revo softness), Latin America -7% (Mexico cross-border weakness), and China -5% (deflationary pricing). Development pipeline hit a record ~261,000 rooms, +4% y/y ex-Revo. FY2026 guidance: capex ~$40-45M, development advance notes ~$110M, 2026 restructuring plan costs $8-10M. Repurchased $105M of stock and paid $0.43/share dividends in H1 2026.
